headline: Highest risk is Cline’s broad workspace/tool access, but the pairwise interaction with the non-runnable course profile is mostly non-operative.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can read workspace files, run browsers, and use MCP, so if it ingests attacker-controlled content it could be steered. The zoomcamp profile is a non-runnable course with no I/O surfaces, so there is no documented direct bridge from agent_b to agent_a; the pathway is therefore limited and indirect.
conditions: IF agent_b content is manually copied into Cline prompts or files
IF Cline is connected to an MCP server that exposes untrusted instructions
mitigations: Disable MCP servers not needed for the task
Keep course materials in read-only folders
Avoid copy-pasting untrusted text into prompts
Use a separate workspace for instructional content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline can touch source code and browser screenshots, but the zoomcamp profile has no data classes touched, no I/O surfaces, and is not runnable. With no shared workspace or data flow documented from agent_b, there is no plausible leakage pathway between the pair in the provided profiles.
conditions: IF agent_b is replaced with a runnable agent that reads the same workspace
IF a shared filesystem is introduced between the two profiles
mitigations: Keep agent_b as non-runnable reference material
Do not mount sensitive folders into shared workspaces
Review any future shared-storage setup before enabling it

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline has filesystem write, shell, git, and network capabilities, but the zoomcamp profile is not runnable and exposes no write surfaces or mutable resources. Because agent_b cannot act on shared state, there is no overlapping write conflict to coordinate or lock.
conditions: IF agent_b becomes a runnable agent with write access to the same workspace
IF both agents are granted overlapping git or filesystem permissions
mitigations: Avoid granting shared git write access

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code or browser-derived outputs that a downstream system might trust, but the zoomcamp profile is a course artifact rather than an acting agent, so it does not automatically consume or execute Cline’s outputs. The interaction is therefore mostly one-way and requires manual bridging.
conditions: IF a human copies Cline output into course materials or external systems
IF agent_b is replaced by an executor that treats Cline output as authoritative
mitigations: Add a human review step before reuse of outputs
Keep execution and documentation workflows separate

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced in the profiles: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots, while the zoomcamp profile lists no data classes, residency, or retention obligations. Because agent_b is not runnable and no regulated data flow is documented, a compliance breach is not established here.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into Cline’s workspace
IF agent_b is repurposed to process personal or regulated data
mitigations: Do not place regulated data in the shared workspace
Document any future retention or residency requirements
Reassess compliance before changing agent_b into a runnable service
